incidents.vector: Voice phishing calls to McKesson employees to steal Okta SSO credentials, then used credentials for unauthorized network access.
incidents.impact: ShinyHunters claims 284 million patient records stolen; company facing extortion demands and refusing to pay ransom; regulatory and legal exposure expected.

incidents.victim: US water utilities, federal agencies (DoL, FERC), medical device company
incidents.vector: Multiple intrusion campaigns directed by IRGC Cyber-Electronic Command targeting OT systems, email infrastructure, and federal agency networks; resumed water sector attacks since late July 2026.
incidents.impact: 100+ water utilities breached across 12 US states; Department of Labor and FERC email accounts compromised; UN organization and medical device company targeted; FBI director's personal email targeted; US offers $10M reward for IRGC-CEC commander Amir Yaryab.

incidents.vector: Voice phishing attack to gain network access; internal documents exfiltrated; ShinyHunters claimed credit.
incidents.impact: More than 7,200 bank customers notified of potential data exposure; company has refused to pay ransom; significant downstream risk to customer financial institutions.

incidents.victim: Serbian civil society — student activists, parliament member, local officials
incidents.vector: NoviSpy and Pegasus spyware deployed on personal devices of political targets; victims alerted by Apple at the end of August; NoviSpy infections attributed to Serbian government authorities.
incidents.impact: At least 14 individuals surveilled including a member of parliament and pro-democracy student protesters; 29 EU Parliament members calling to slow Serbia's EU accession pending investigation.

incidents.victim: Mexican federal agencies, water utilities, transportation firms; Brazilian financial sector
incidents.vector: Two coordinated campaigns (CL-CRI-1131, CL-CRI-1163) using living-off-the-land techniques, self-hosted AI tools (NextChat) for operational troubleshooting, custom remote access trojans, and SOCKS5 proxy tunneling.
incidents.impact: Ongoing data exfiltration from Mexican government and transportation networks active since early 2026; Brazilian financial institutions targeted with custom malware; attackers using AI to overcome operational obstacles in real time.

incidents.vector: Breached a public API endpoint, then deployed frontier AI agents that autonomously mapped the network, harvested credentials, hijacked CI/CD pipelines, and commandeered the victim's own AI infrastructure — compressing a multi-week intrusion into under 10 hours.
incidents.impact: Source code, master credentials, and cloud access keys stolen; CI/CD pipeline hijacked; victim's AI endpoints turned into post-compromise infrastructure; attackers left an 80-page security audit; ransomware negotiations underway.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of two zero-day vulnerabilities in SonicWall SMA1000 remote access appliances: CVE-2026-83548 (server-side request forgery) and CVE-2026-83549 (OS command injection).
incidents.impact: CISA added both CVEs to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Sep 2; federal agencies required to patch within mandated deadline; organizations with internet-exposed SMA1000 appliances at risk of full remote compromise.

incidents.victim: IDScan.net — 153 million US and Canadian residents
incidents.vector: Sustained breach of IDScan.net systems, which scan and store driver's licenses for enterprise clients including Hertz, Target, FedEx, Caesars Entertainment, and cannabis dispensaries; data continuously exfiltrated over an extended period.
incidents.impact: 153M+ US and Canadian driver's license scans — including infrared and UV versions revealing security features — sold on a Russian cybercrime forum via the 'Nexus' identity theft service; includes current government officials; FBI investigation opened; exfiltration ongoing.

incidents.vector: Mass password recovery attack targeting hundreds of thousands of X accounts, aimed at pivoting to the X Money digital banking service.
incidents.impact: Attack mitigated; company reports no accounts were compromised; DOJ actively investigating; highlights risk to users as X expands into financial services.

incidents.victim: Coder (developer cloud infrastructure tools) and downstream customers
incidents.vector: Hackers compromised Coder's Cloudflare infrastructure to insert malicious registry servers that served tampered Terraform modules to developers building AI cloud infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Malicious Terraform modules delivered for approximately 14 hours on August 31; downstream risk to cloud AI infrastructure built using poisoned modules; full scope of exposure under investigation.

incidents.victim: Government and diplomatic organizations in Romania, Spain, Turkey; defense manufacturing
incidents.vector: Spearphishing with macro-enabled Word documents using diplomatic lures — including impersonation of Spain's Ministry of the Presidency — to deploy the HOOKEDGE batch-script backdoor; command-and-control routed through legitimate webhook services to blend with normal traffic.
incidents.impact: European government, diplomatic, and defense manufacturing targets in Romania, Spain, and Turkey compromised with persistent backdoor from September 2025 through April 2026; intelligence collection aligned with Russian interests in Moldovan elections and NATO-adjacent governance.

incidents.victim: Global software supply chain — thousands of businesses worldwide
incidents.vector: Embedded malicious code in hundreds of open-source tools using the Shai-Hulud self-propagating worm; stole developer credentials to publish malicious package versions that spread through downstream builds and corporate CI/CD pipelines.
incidents.impact: Corporate cloud environments compromised globally; widespread data extortion campaign; Australian Federal Police arrested two alleged leaders — Ruben Thomson, 21, and Louis Gaebler, 23 — in Perth; supply chain operation reported as ongoing despite arrests.

incidents.victim: US critical infrastructure (targeted); Chinese botnet platforms disrupted
incidents.vector: Operated QScan and QTRouter botnet platforms — run by Chinese company Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology for QTFY hacking group — to enable state-sponsored targeting of US critical infrastructure; platforms used hard-coded domains enabling court-authorized seizure.
incidents.impact: DOJ and FBI seized command-and-control infrastructure via court order on August 26; Chinese state-sponsored targeting of US critical infrastructure disrupted but broader campaign threat remains active.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized intrusion into TVING platform systems; breach method not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Approximately 40 million user accounts compromised; 70+ types of personal data stolen including names, emails, and phone numbers; company disclosed the incident in September — a day past the reporting deadline — and faces a regulatory fine; offering ~$15 compensation per user.

incidents.vector: External Microsoft Teams accounts impersonating IT helpdesk staff initiated vishing calls (campaign tracked as 'Spring Ring'), coercing employees to install remote management tools or custom malware; advanced variant used NTLM relay attacks to target domain controllers.
incidents.impact: Remote access to victim systems obtained across multiple companies over a four-month campaign; domain-level compromise attempted in advanced variant cases; campaign active January through April 2026.
